project.name: flash-research-api
project.description: Flash Research Platform backend: FastAPI API + worker for momentum-trading market intelligence (NYSE/NASDAQ scanning, quantitative metrics, real-time dashboard).

nodes.name: base.py
nodes.summary: Defines the abstract MarketDataProvider port (hexagonal architecture) that all market data adapters must implement, decoupling the rest of the system from any specific data vendor.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Python's ABC + abstractmethod to define a hexagonal-architecture port; concrete vendor adapters (e.g. PolygonAdapter) implement this contract.

nodes.name: MarketDataProvider
nodes.summary: Abstract port interface declaring list_instruments and get_eod_bars contracts that concrete market data provider adapters must implement.

nodes.name: polygon.py
nodes.summary: Concrete adapter implementing MarketDataProvider for Polygon.io, handling paginated instrument listing, adjusted/unadjusted EOD bar fetching, and translation of Polygon's raw JSON into canonical InstrumentDTO/OHLCVBar schemas.
nodes.languageNotes: Separates a pure translation layer (_parse_instruments, _merge_bars, module-level helpers) from the networked layer (_get, _get_aggs) to keep the fixture-based unit tests free of HTTP calls.

nodes.name: PolygonAdapter
nodes.summary: Concrete MarketDataProvider adapter for Polygon.io; manages a reused httpx.Client, paginates the reference tickers endpoint via cursor, fetches adjusted and unadjusted daily aggregates, and merges them into canonical OHLCVBar records keyed by timestamp.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Barrel module re-exporting the canonical InstrumentDTO, OHLCVBar, and Quote schemas as the package's public schema API.

nodes.name: instrument.py
nodes.summary: Defines the canonical, provider-agnostic InstrumentDTO pydantic model representing a tradable instrument, used as the common shape between data providers and the downstream catalog job.

nodes.name: InstrumentDTO
nodes.summary: Immutable pydantic DTO representing a canonical tradable instrument with normalized exchange, raw provider type, and active status.

nodes.name: market.py
nodes.summary: Defines canonical OHLCVBar and Quote pydantic models for market data, using Decimal for monetary precision and validating OHLCV sanity (high >= low, non-negative volume).
nodes.languageNotes: Uses pydantic's model_validator(mode="after") to enforce cross-field invariants, and Decimal fields throughout to avoid float imprecision on prices.

nodes.name: OHLCVBar
nodes.summary: Immutable pydantic DTO for a canonical daily OHLCV bar with Decimal pricing and a post-validation sanity check (high >= low, non-negative volume).

nodes.name: Quote
nodes.summary: Immutable pydantic DTO representing a point-in-time price quote with change percentage, volume, and timestamp.

nodes.name: test_polygon_adapter.py
nodes.summary: Unit test suite for PolygonAdapter covering instrument parsing, adjusted/unadjusted bar merging, Decimal precision, pagination limits, and HTTP error handling, using respx-mocked responses and JSON fixtures.

nodes.name: test_parse_instruments_maps_exchange_and_active
nodes.summary: Verifies PolygonAdapter._parse_instruments correctly maps Polygon MIC codes to internal exchange enums and preserves each instrument's active status.

nodes.name: test_merge_bars_uses_raw_close_and_adjusted_adj_close
nodes.summary: Verifies _merge_bars combines the raw close price from unadjusted data with the adj_close price from adjusted data into canonical OHLCVBar records.

nodes.name: test_merge_bars_matches_by_timestamp
nodes.summary: Verifies _merge_bars pairs unadjusted and adjusted bars by their epoch-ms timestamp rather than by list order.

nodes.name: test_get_eod_bars_calls_both_adjusted_and_unadjusted
nodes.summary: Verifies get_eod_bars issues both adjusted and unadjusted HTTP requests via respx mocks and correctly merges the two responses into OHLCVBar records.

nodes.name: test_list_instruments_respects_max_pages
nodes.summary: Verifies list_instruments stops paginating once max_pages is reached even when Polygon's response indicates more pages are available.

nodes.name: env.py
nodes.summary: Alembic migration environment script that loads DATABASE_URL from the environment, wires SQLAlchemy's Base.metadata as the migration target, and dispatches to offline or online migration execution.
nodes.languageNotes: Standard Alembic env.py pattern: offline mode emits SQL against a URL-only config, online mode opens a real DB connection via engine_from_config before running migrations.

nodes.name: run_migrations_offline
nodes.summary: Configures Alembic to emit migration SQL using literal bind values without opening a live database connection ('offline' mode).

nodes.name: run_migrations_online
nodes.summary: Creates a SQLAlchemy engine from the Alembic config, opens a live connection, and runs migrations directly against the database ('online' mode).

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Package barrel for the core ORM models, re-exporting Base, Instrument, and Profile as the public surface of packages.core.models.

nodes.name: base.py
nodes.summary: Defines the SQLAlchemy DeclarativeBase subclass that all ORM models inherit from, whose metadata registry is consumed by Alembic for autogenerate.

nodes.name: Base
nodes.summary: SQLAlchemy declarative base class; its metadata attribute tracks all mapped tables and is linked to Alembic's target_metadata for migration autogeneration.

nodes.name: instrument.py
nodes.summary: Defines the Instrument ORM model, the catalog of tradable tickers (ticker, exchange, sector, active/delisted status) with constraints and indexes for the market-scanning universe.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses SQLAlchemy 2.0-style Mapped/mapped_column typing, a CheckConstraint restricting exchange to NYSE/NASDAQ/AMEX/OTHER, and a partial index on is_active to keep delisted-but-retained rows (avoiding survivorship bias) queryable efficiently.

nodes.name: Instrument
nodes.summary: ORM model for the instruments table: the ticker catalog keyed by ticker symbol, tracking exchange, sector/industry classification, and active/delisted lifecycle without ever deleting rows.

nodes.name: profile.py
nodes.summary: Defines the Profile ORM model, a 1:1 user profile linked to the auth user, storing display name and app settings as JSONB.

nodes.name: Profile
nodes.summary: ORM model for the profiles table: a UUID-keyed, 1:1 extension of the auth user holding display name and JSONB app preferences.

nodes.name: main.py
nodes.summary: FastAPI application entry point that instantiates the app and registers the health router.
nodes.languageNotes: Minimal FastAPI bootstrap file; app composition happens by including routers rather than defining routes directly.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Empty package marker file that makes apps/api/routers importable as a Python package.

nodes.name: health.py
nodes.summary: Defines the health-check and root API routes used to verify the service is running.

nodes.name: test_health.py
nodes.summary: Integration test that exercises the FastAPI app via TestClient to confirm the /health endpoint returns a 200 status with the expected payload.

nodes.name: health_check
nodes.summary: Async handler for GET /health that returns a simple status-ok JSON response for readiness/liveness checks.

nodes.name: root
nodes.summary: Async handler for GET / that returns a welcome message confirming the Flash Research API is running.

nodes.name: test_health_returns_ok
nodes.summary: Test case asserting the /health endpoint responds with HTTP 200 and a JSON body of {"status": "ok"}.

nodes.name: ci.yml
nodes.summary: GitHub Actions CI workflow ("backend-ci") that spins up a TimescaleDB service container and runs dependency sync, linting, database migrations, and the test suite on every pull request and push to main.
nodes.languageNotes: Single-job pipeline using a Postgres/TimescaleDB service container with health checks and uv for fast Python dependency management; database migrations (alembic) run before tests to validate schema changes in CI.

nodes.name: lint-test
nodes.summary: CI job that runs on ubuntu-latest with a TimescaleDB Postgres service container, executing dependency install, lint, migration, and test steps against DATABASE_URL and REDIS_URL environment variables.

nodes.name: uv sync
nodes.summary: Installs project dependencies using the uv package manager as the first execution step of the CI job.

nodes.name: uv run ruff check .
nodes.summary: Runs the ruff linter across the whole repository to enforce Python code style and catch static errors before merge.

nodes.name: uv run alembic upgrade head
nodes.summary: Applies all pending Alembic database migrations against the TimescaleDB service container to validate schema migrations in CI.

nodes.name: uv run pytest
nodes.summary: Runs the project's pytest test suite as the final verification step of the CI pipeline.

nodes.name: .env.example
nodes.summary: Template for local environment variables (DATABASE_URL, REDIS_URL, DEBUG, POLYGON_API_KEY) that must be copied to .env and match the docker-compose services for local development.
nodes.languageNotes: DATABASE_URL and REDIS_URL values are hard-coded to match the credentials and ports defined in docker-compose.yml.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Project overview and onboarding guide for the Flash Research API backend, covering the tech stack, local setup steps (uv sync, docker compose up, alembic upgrade), common commands, repo structure, and data conventions (numeric prices, no hard deletes for delisted instruments, Alembic-only schema changes).

nodes.name: alembic.ini
nodes.summary: Alembic migration tool configuration; sets the migration script location to migrations/ (via the %(here)s token) and leaves most options at their generic, commented-out defaults.

nodes.name: docker-compose.yml
nodes.summary: Docker Compose definition for local infrastructure: a TimescaleDB-on-Postgres 17 database service and a Redis 7 cache/bus service, each with health checks and persistent named volumes.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses named volumes (flash_db_data, flash_redis_data) so `docker compose down` preserves data unless run with -v.

nodes.name: db
nodes.summary: TimescaleDB (Postgres 17) service exposing port 5432 with user flash / password flash_dev_pw / database flash_research, backed by a persistent volume and a pg_isready health check.

nodes.name: redis
nodes.summary: Redis 7 (alpine) service exposing port 6379 for caching/messaging, backed by a persistent volume and a redis-cli ping health check.

nodes.name: pyproject.toml
nodes.summary: Python project manifest for flash-research-api defining runtime dependencies (FastAPI, SQLAlchemy, Alembic, asyncpg, psycopg2-binary, pydantic-settings, uvicorn), dev dependencies (pytest, ruff, respx), and tool configuration for Ruff linting and pytest.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses PEP 735 dependency-groups for dev dependencies and configures ruff lint rule sets (E, F, I, UP, B, SIM) with first-party import grouping for apps/packages.

nodes.name: polygon_aggs_adjusted.json
nodes.summary: Static mock response fixture representing a Polygon.io aggregates (OHLCV bars) API reply with adjusted=true, used to stub network calls when testing the split/dividend-adjusted price path of the Polygon adapter.

nodes.name: polygon_aggs_unadjusted.json
nodes.summary: Static mock response fixture representing a Polygon.io aggregates (OHLCV bars) API reply with adjusted=false, used to stub network calls when testing the raw (unadjusted) price path of the Polygon adapter.

nodes.name: polygon_tickers.json
nodes.summary: Static mock response fixture listing sample Polygon.io tickers (active/delisted equities, a non-US-exchange listing, and an ETF) used to test ticker-universe filtering logic in the Polygon adapter without hitting the live API.

nodes.name: .python-version
nodes.summary: Pins the project's Python interpreter version (3.13) for version managers such as pyenv and uv.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Empty package marker turning `apps` into a Python package containing the API and worker applications.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Empty package marker turning `apps.api` into a Python package for the FastAPI application code.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Empty package marker turning `apps.api.core` into a Python package for core API infrastructure such as settings.

nodes.name: config.py
nodes.summary: Defines the Settings class (pydantic-settings) that loads database, Redis, debug, and Polygon.io API configuration from environment variables / .env, and exposes a module-level `settings` singleton used across the app.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses pydantic-settings BaseSettings with SettingsConfigDict to auto-load a .env file into typed fields.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Empty package marker turning `apps.worker` into a Python package for the background worker process.

nodes.name: main.py
nodes.summary: Worker process entry point; configures basic logging and logs a startup message when run directly as a script.

nodes.name: README
nodes.summary: Minimal Alembic README noting this is a generic single-database migration environment configuration.

nodes.name: script.py.mako
nodes.summary: Alembic Mako template used to scaffold new migration revision files, generating the revision metadata header plus empty upgrade/downgrade function stubs.
nodes.languageNotes: Mako templating syntax (${...}) is interpolated by Alembic's `revision` command to produce concrete migration scripts like 0001_initial_schema.py.

nodes.name: 0001_initial_schema.py
nodes.summary: Initial Alembic migration that enables the TimescaleDB extension and creates the `profiles` and `instruments` tables with update-timestamp triggers, indexes, and row-level security policies restricting profile access to the owning user while allowing public read of the instrument catalog.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses raw SQL via op.execute() rather than Alembic's declarative op.create_table/op.add_column helpers, including Postgres-specific RLS policies and a trigger function.

nodes.name: 0002_add_instrument_type.py
nodes.summary: Alembic migration adding a nullable `type` text column to the `instruments` table to capture the data provider's raw instrument classification (e.g. common stock, ETF, ADR) for universe filtering.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Empty package marker turning `packages.core` into a Python package for shared core infrastructure (db, providers).

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Empty package marker turning `packages.core.db` into a Python package for database session and engine setup.

nodes.name: session.py
nodes.summary: Defines the shared async SQLAlchemy engine and session factory (asyncpg driver) intended for use by the API and worker processes, forcing the async driver scheme even if DATABASE_URL specifies the sync `postgresql://` form used by Alembic.
nodes.languageNotes: Alembic's env.py uses the sync psycopg2 driver while this module rewrites the URL to postgresql+asyncpg:// for runtime async access, keeping migrations and app code on separate drivers.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Empty package marker turning `packages.core.providers` into a Python package for market data provider adapters.

nodes.name: smoke_polygon.py
nodes.summary: Manual smoke-test script that exercises the Polygon adapter against the live Polygon.io API, fetching EOD bars for AAPL and listing active instruments to visually verify the integration works end-to-end.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Empty package marker turning `tests` into a Python package for the project's test suite.

nodes.name: profiles
nodes.summary: User profile table (1:1 with an auth user) storing display name and a JSONB settings blob, protected by row-level security policies that scope select/update/insert to the owning user.

nodes.name: instruments
nodes.summary: Public catalog of tradable instruments (ticker, name, exchange, sector, industry, active/delisted status) with RLS allowing public read access; rows are never deleted, only marked inactive, to avoid survivorship bias in backtests.

nodes.name: Settings
nodes.summary: Pydantic-settings model declaring the application's typed configuration fields (database_url, redis_url, debug, Polygon API key/base URL) loaded from environment variables or a .env file.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Worker entry-point function that logs a startup message; invoked when the module is run as `__main__`.

nodes.name: upgrade
nodes.summary: Applies the initial schema forward: enables TimescaleDB, creates the updated_at trigger function, creates `profiles` and `instruments` tables with indexes and triggers, and enables row-level security policies on both tables.

nodes.name: downgrade
nodes.summary: Reverses the initial schema migration by dropping RLS policies, disabling RLS, and dropping the `instruments`/`profiles` tables and the trigger function.

nodes.name: upgrade
nodes.summary: Adds a nullable `type` text column to the `instruments` table to record the provider's raw instrument classification.

nodes.name: downgrade
nodes.summary: Reverses the migration by dropping the `type` column from the `instruments` table.

nodes.name: _async_url
nodes.summary: Reads DATABASE_URL from the environment (falling back to a local dev default) and rewrites the `postgresql://` scheme to `postgresql+asyncpg://` so the runtime engine always uses the async driver, distinct from Alembic's sync driver.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Entry point that validates a Polygon API key is configured, then uses PolygonAdapter to fetch EOD bars for AAPL and list active instruments, printing results for manual verification.

layers.name: Application Layer
layers.description: The two deployable Python processes (FastAPI API and the background worker) — app bootstrap, health-check routing, and pydantic-settings configuration that expose and configure the market-scanning service.

layers.name: Market Data Provider Layer
layers.description: The hexagonal port/adapter boundary for external market data — the abstract MarketDataProvider port and the concrete Polygon.io adapter that translates vendor JSON into canonical shapes, decoupling the rest of the system from any single data vendor.

layers.name: Schema / DTO Layer
layers.description: Canonical, provider-agnostic pydantic data shapes (InstrumentDTO, OHLCVBar, Quote) that form the common contract between the market data provider adapters and downstream consumers.

layers.name: Data Layer
layers.description: Persistence for the market-scanning universe: SQLAlchemy ORM models, the shared async DB session factory, and the Alembic migration history (including the TimescaleDB-backed instruments and profiles tables) that define and evolve the schema.

layers.name: Testing Layer
layers.description: Automated pytest coverage for the Polygon adapter and API health check, their JSON response fixtures, and the manual smoke-test script used to exercise the Polygon adapter against the live API.

layers.name: Infrastructure & Configuration
layers.description: Root-level project setup: local TimescaleDB/Redis containers (docker-compose), environment variable and Alembic templates, Python dependency manifest and interpreter pin, and the top-level README onboarding guide.

layers.name: CI/CD Pipeline
layers.description: The GitHub Actions backend-ci workflow and its ordered job steps (dependency sync, lint, migration apply, test run) that gate every pull request against a TimescaleDB service container.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: README.md introduces Flash Research as a momentum-trading intelligence platform for NYSE/NASDAQ market scanning, quantitative metrics, and a real-time dashboard. It explains that the repo hosts two deployables sharing code — the FastAPI-based `apps/api` and the batch-oriented `apps/worker` — plus `packages/core`, a shared library of models, schemas, and providers. It also lays out the stack (Python 3.12+, FastAPI, SQLAlchemy 2.x, Alembic, PostgreSQL 17 + TimescaleDB, Redis 7, uv, Docker Compose) and two hard conventions the rest of the tour will keep bumping into: prices are always `numeric`/`Decimal`, never `float`, and delisted instruments are marked inactive rather than deleted to avoid survivorship bias.

tour.title: API Entry Point
tour.description: apps/api/main.py is where the FastAPI application object is created and wired up — it is the top of the dependency graph for the API process and the file the README's `uvicorn apps.api.main:app` command actually boots. Right now its only job is to instantiate the app and register the health router, keeping the entry point thin and letting the real logic live in packages/core. This mirrors the README's description of `apps/api` as 'the HTTP face' of the platform.

tour.title: Health Check Routes
tour.description: apps/api/routers/health.py defines the first (and currently only) set of HTTP routes, exposed through the empty routers/__init__.py package marker and registered by main.py from Step 2. tests/test_health.py exercises this wiring end-to-end using FastAPI's TestClient, hitting /health through the real app object rather than mocking it out — a pattern worth noticing before we look at how the Polygon adapter is tested differently in Step 8.

tour.title: Application Settings
tour.description: apps/api/core/config.py centralizes configuration using pydantic-settings, loading the database URL, Redis URL, debug flag, and Polygon API key from environment variables. It has the third-highest fan-in in the codebase, meaning multiple parts of the system (and, as you'll see in Step 12, docker-compose's db and redis services) depend on this single source of truth for connection details rather than reading `os.environ` directly.
tour.languageLesson: pydantic-settings maps environment variables onto a typed class at import time, giving you validation and autocomplete for config values instead of untyped dict lookups — a common pattern for 12-factor-style Python services.

tour.title: The Market Data Port
tour.description: packages/core/providers/base.py defines MarketDataProvider, an abstract interface that any market data vendor adapter must implement. This is the 'port' half of a hexagonal (ports-and-adapters) architecture: the rest of the system depends on this abstraction, not on any specific vendor's API shape, which is what lets Polygon.io be swapped for another provider later without touching downstream code.
tour.languageLesson: Hexagonal architecture inverts the usual dependency direction: instead of business logic depending on a vendor SDK, the vendor adapter depends on an interface (port) that the business logic defines. In Python this is typically an abc.ABC or typing.Protocol.

tour.title: Canonical Data Shapes
tour.description: The MarketDataProvider port from Step 5 speaks in terms of canonical, provider-agnostic pydantic models rather than raw vendor JSON: InstrumentDTO (instrument.py) and OHLCVBar/Quote (market.py), re-exported through schemas/__init__.py as the package's public API. Note that market.py uses Decimal rather than float for prices and volumes — the direct code-level enforcement of the README's 'never float for money' convention from Step 1.
tour.languageLesson: pydantic models validate and coerce data at the boundary of the system. Using Decimal instead of float for monetary fields avoids binary floating-point rounding errors that would silently corrupt price calculations.

tour.title: The Polygon.io Adapter
tour.description: packages/core/providers/polygon.py is the concrete adapter implementing the MarketDataProvider port from Step 5 for Polygon.io — the highest fan-out file in the codebase after README.md, since it pulls in both the port and the canonical schemas from Step 6. It handles paginated instrument listing and adjusted/unadjusted end-of-day bar fetching, translating Polygon's raw JSON responses into the InstrumentDTO and OHLCVBar shapes the rest of the system expects.

tour.title: Testing the Adapter
tour.description: tests/test_polygon_adapter.py has the highest fan-in of any file in the codebase, pulling together the Polygon adapter from Step 7 and three JSON fixtures capturing real Polygon response shapes: adjusted aggregates, unadjusted aggregates, and a tickers listing. Using respx to mock HTTP responses rather than hitting the live API keeps these tests fast and deterministic while still validating the adapter's JSON-to-DTO translation logic against realistic payloads.
tour.languageLesson: respx intercepts httpx requests at the transport layer, letting tests assert exact outbound calls and return canned JSON fixtures — useful for adapters that wrap third-party HTTP APIs, since it tests the real serialization/deserialization code path without network flakiness.

tour.title: ORM Models
tour.description: packages/core/models defines the persistence layer with SQLAlchemy: base.py's DeclarativeBase is the shared root that Instrument and Profile both inherit from, re-exported together through models/__init__.py. These models are the database-backed counterparts to the InstrumentDTO from Step 6 — the DTO is what providers speak, the ORM model is what gets persisted — and instrument.py's constraints and indexes encode the README's 'never delete, only deactivate' rule at the schema level.
tour.languageLesson: SQLAlchemy 2.x's DeclarativeBase replaces the older declarative_base() factory function with a class you subclass directly, giving better static-typing support for ORM models.

tour.title: Database Session Factory
tour.description: packages/core/db/session.py provides a shared async SQLAlchemy engine and session factory built on asyncpg, used by both the API and worker processes so neither has to configure its own database connection independently. It's configured by the same docker-compose 'db' service you'll see in Step 12, and it's the runtime counterpart to the models defined in Step 9 — the engine that actually executes queries against those ORM classes.

tour.title: Schema Migrations
tour.description: migrations/env.py wires the models/__init__.py barrel from Step 9 into Alembic as the migration target, so schema changes are always generated from the ORM models rather than written by hand — enforcing the README's 'schema changes only through Alembic' rule. 0001_initial_schema.py creates the TimescaleDB extension, the profiles table (row-level security scoping data to its owning user) and instruments table (the public, append-only catalog behind Step 9's is_active flag), while 0002_add_instrument_type.py layers on a nullable type column, showing how the schema evolves incrementally in production.
tour.languageLesson: Alembic migrations are ordered, incremental Python scripts with an upgrade()/downgrade() pair. Each new migration should be additive and reversible so the schema can move forward or backward without manual SQL intervention.

tour.title: Local Infrastructure & Config
tour.description: docker-compose.yml stands up the TimescaleDB and Redis services that back the session factory (Step 10) and settings (Step 4) locally, while .env.example is the template developers copy to .env to point the app at those services — matching the README's five-step 'from zero' setup. alembic.ini and pyproject.toml round out the project's configuration surface: the former points Alembic at the right database and script location, the latter declares Python dependencies plus Ruff/pytest tool config.
tour.languageLesson: Docker Compose service names (db, redis) become DNS hostnames other containers can reach on the shared network, which is why the DATABASE_URL and REDIS_URL in .env.example reference them by name rather than by IP or localhost.

tour.title: The Worker Process
tour.description: apps/worker/main.py is the entry point for the second deployable the README describes — the process meant to handle ingestion and batch calculations. Today it's a skeleton that only logs startup, but it already shares packages/core's providers, schemas, models, and db session with the API, so the momentum-scanning and metrics logic the README promises will slot in here without duplicating any of the persistence or data-provider code you've just walked through.

tour.title: Continuous Integration
tour.description: The GitHub Actions workflow in .github/workflows/ci.yml is what actually gates every pull request: it syncs dependencies, lints with Ruff, runs the Alembic migrations from Step 11 against a real TimescaleDB service container, and then runs the pytest suites from Steps 3 and 8. Running migrations in CI (rather than just linting the migration files) catches schema drift and broken migrations before they reach the docker-compose environment from Step 12 or production.
tour.languageLesson: GitHub Actions service containers (like a TimescaleDB container defined under `services:`) run alongside the job's steps for the duration of the workflow, giving CI a real, ephemeral database instead of mocking the DB layer — trading a slower pipeline for higher-fidelity integration tests.
